evidence_items.explanation: Shows that as of the post date the 118th Congress had passed no AI provisions at all. The first came in the NDAA, passed December 18.

receipt.public_excerpt: it does not include generally applicable provisions, for example, the comprehensive AI legislation that the Bipartisan Senate AI Working Group and other members called for this year

receipt.public_excerpt: Sacks’ appointment is widely viewed as a sign that the Trump administration will fulfill its campaign promises to take a pro-industry, deregulatory stance on AI.

evidence_items.explanation: A week before the post, a Silicon Valley investor who opposes AI regulation was named White House AI czar. That is a gain in influence for the anti-regulation camp.

receipt.public_excerpt: Many powerful players in Silicon Valley, including venture capital firm Andreessen Horowitz, OpenAI and trade groups representing Google and Meta, lobbied against the bill

evidence_items.explanation: Andreessen Horowitz lobbied against California's SB 1047, which Newsom vetoed. That is a policy win for Andreessen's side in 2024.

unresolved_gaps: Congress did pass some defense-focused AI provisions in the December 2024 NDAA. These do not regulate AI generally.
